newsitem.title: UK: UK's HGCA sees tight breadmaking wheat supplies.
newsitem.headline: UK's HGCA sees tight breadmaking wheat supplies.

text.p: UK breadmaking wheat is likely to be in short supply this season as more feed varieties are likely to have been harvested, according to the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA).

Final seed certification figures for the UK showed a six percent rise in wheat certifications, but breadmaking varieties represented a smaller proportion of the total compared with last year's figures.
Higher yields recorded this year should help to partly offset the reduced milling wheat area and there is also the carryover from last year, but the HGCA said high quality wheat would be tight.

"It is clear that good quality breadwheat supplies are tight, particularly given the lower protein values recorded from this year's harvest, which could lead to increased imports," the HGCA said in its weekly digest.
Barley certifications rose 10 percent in a second consecutive sharp increase. Malting barley certifications increased by the same percentange.
"The high yield from this year's barley harvest and reasonable quality (apart from high screenings) should allow for adequate malting barley supplies this season," said the HGCA.
The National Farmers Union (NFU) on Tuesday estimated the 1996 UK grain harvest 10 percent higher from 1995 at 24.09 million tonnes, with wheat put at 15.78 million tonnes and barley at 7.68 million.
But a breakdown of wheat types was not provided.
